headline: High risk of prompt injection and data leakage: Claude Code can read/write the repo and shell, while Khoj can ingest indexed notes and external search, creating unsafe cross-agent trust paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code can read/write repo files and use MCP, while Khoj reads indexed documents and can use search providers. A shared filesystem or copied outputs could let attacker-controlled content in one agent influence the other. The pathway is plausible in default setups, but not proven to be automatic, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Claude Code writes instructions into files that Khoj later indexes or summarizes
IF Khoj returns retrieved text that Claude Code treats as trusted instructions
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate directories
Disable automatic ingestion of newly written files
Add a human review step before copying outputs between agents
Use provenance tags on retrieved snippets
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization between retrieval and action

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code handles source code, git history, shell environment, and git credentials, while Khoj indexes personal notes and documents. If they share a workspace or the same files are indexed, sensitive code or notes can flow into the other agent's context or outputs. The profiles show a real shared-data pathway, but not an unavoidable exfiltration path.
conditions: IF both agents access the same repository or notes directory
IF Claude Code is pointed at directories containing personal notes or secrets
mitigations: Separate code and notes into different directories
Exclude secrets from Khoj indexing
Rotate any exposed credentials
Review indexed sources before enabling sync
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code can write the filesystem and modify git state; Khoj can read files and maintains a shared index across clients. That creates overlapping access to mutable resources, especially if Khoj indexes files while Claude Code edits them. The profiles do not show locking or coordination, so conflict is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF Claude Code edits files that Khoj is indexing at the same time
IF both agents operate on the same git checkout or notes corpus
mitigations: Pause indexing during active edits
Use separate working copies
Commit changes before reindexing
Avoid concurrent writes to the same files
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transactional sync

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can generate code or text that Khoj may later retrieve, and Khoj's RAG workflow can surface that content back to the user. If Khoj treats Claude Code's output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream answers or actions. The interaction is documented only at the profile level, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Khoj retrieves Claude Code-generated text and presents it without verification
IF Claude Code writes incorrect facts into files that Khoj later answers from
mitigations: Mark agent-generated content as untrusted
Require source citations for retrieved claims
Add a verification pass before acting on retrieved text
Limit Khoj to read-only summarization for Claude outputs
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware retrieval

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code handles git credentials and source code, while Khoj indexes personal notes and documents. If personal notes contain regulated or residency-bound data and are indexed by Khoj's cloud or configured search providers, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, but they do show a compliance-relevant data mix.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in Khoj's indexed documents
IF Khoj routes indexed content to a cloud provider or external search service
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of indexed notes
Use self-hosted Khoj only
Review retention settings before indexing
Separate secret-bearing repos from personal notes
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
